note: Ad-hoc prompt-read A/B, not the standard benchmark protocol (docs/BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md): the fixtures here are synthetic seeded paragraphs, not the frozen standard-v1 corpus. The authoritative number is always the engine's own log line 'prompt N tokens = R reused + F read in T ms (X tok/s)'.

hardware.gpu: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT 20 GB (gfx1100), driver 32.0.32029.2010, WDDM
hardware.hip: amdhip64_7.dll; source builds made against ROCm 10.2 (TheRock) wheels on Windows

method.per_run: one fresh engine process, one cold unique prompt of the target size, max_tokens=8, greedy; the learned expert-profile is redirected to a throwaway copy so the synthetic routing never writes the real table
method.prompt: seeded synthetic paragraphs (the same generator and seed inside a pack), chars/token calibrated with a small probe first, so the token count of each arm lands within ~0.5% of the target but the prompts are not byte-identical across arms
method.pairing: arms alternate stock/patched across the session, so machine drift shows up between halves
method.validity_check: before a number is used, the run's RAM-residency line must match the session norm: 'complement ready: resident X GiB, pinned X GiB' with the two equal, or 'N ranges registered (M MiB), the cap was reached'. One patched run (X2) and both headroom-2 runs were caught by this check: X2 had 436 ranges / 4356 MiB ('the driver refused the next one') and was thrown out; the headroom runs pinned 0.00 GiB.
